transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. [Name]. Well, I came in because... I just feel wound up almost all day long. It's like my body is constantly bracing for something to happen. Even when I'm just sitting at my computer for work, or trying to relax after dinner, I just can't seem to shake this tension.
How long have you been feeling this constant tension and 'wound up' sensation—has it been going on for weeks, or more like several months or longer?

It's definitely been longer than a few weeks. I'd say it's actually been going on for about thirteen months now. That was right around the time my sister in Arecibo started needing a lot more help from the family, so... yeah, it's been a little over a year of feeling like this.

Would you say this tension and worry is mostly about your sister's situation, or do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different things—like work, health, or other family matters—as well?

It's not just my sister, no. I mean, she's definitely on my mind, but... my mind really just keeps going from one concern to another. I'll be thinking about her in Arecibo, and then suddenly I'm worrying about whether I missed an email or something at the office, or if my husband is safe driving home. 

Then it shifts to my church commitments, or the bills, or... well, just about anything. It's a lot of different things, and I always find myself preparing for problems that haven't even happened yet.
Along with this constant worry, have you noticed physical symptoms like muscle tension, feeling easily fatigued, restlessness, or trouble sleeping?

Yes, trouble sleeping is definitely one of them. I mean, most nights I do fall asleep eventually. But then I wake up around three or four in the morning, and my mind just starts going. I'll find myself thinking about my sister’s next appointment, or worrying about some server issue at work. And... well, even when I manage to get enough hours of sleep on paper, I start the morning feeling like I never really rested at all.
Besides the sleep trouble, have you noticed feeling physically restless or on edge, having muscle tension, or having trouble concentrating during the day?

Yes, definitely the restlessness and tension. That's actually the main reason I came in to see you. I just feel wound up almost all day long. It's like my body is constantly bracing for something bad to happen, even when there's no reason for it. I'll just be sitting at my computer at work, or trying to relax on the couch after dinner, and I still have that on-edge, tense feeling in my muscles.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports excessive, uncontrollable worry about multiple domains (sister's health, work, spouse's safety, finances, church) persisting for approximately 13 months, exceeding the 6-month duration threshold for GAD. Associated symptoms include sleep disturbance (early waking with racing thoughts, non-restorative sleep), muscle tension, and pervasive restlessness/feeling on-edge. Worry is not confined to a single stressor (e.g., sister's caregiving needs) but generalizes across life domains, distinguishing this from an adjustment disorder. No indication of trauma-related re-experiencing, avoidance, or hypervigilance specific to a traumatic event, making PTSD/Acute stress less likely. The chronicity, multiplicity of worry domains, and associated somatic/cognitive symptoms support a diagnosis of Generalized Anxiety Disorder.
